items.note: S2.1/S2.2 follow the proof: net change (JV+RG)x independent of scratch, side wires cancel unwanted |S∩T| coefficients, three stages give (x,y+x),(-y,y+x),(-y,x). But h=100, the triple index set, the neighbour rules and the actual coefficients (|S∩T| mod 2, (|S∩T|-1)/2) are never given, so the cancellation itself is not shown.

S2.3 states that the network on arrays implements D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1}, so each route applies only its endpoint frames, and quotes the commuting argument at line 812. It is a single infer step with no derivation beyond the quote.

S2.4 gives nondegenerate nested labels in an m-dimensional bilinear space, with the only decreasing edges the central wires from time 3 to 4, and S2.5 gives L/N<1/2. The loss h per edge, L=Ich, the budget Wm-2N+2L, the exact ratios 100/539 and 101/539, and the triple-indicator/F^{⊗3} construction are all missing.
S4.3 states the endpoint matrices differ by I_m, the shear is H<-H+D on every role, and s_b<W_b m. It does not give the projection assignment with the -P_{U_a} source matrices, or s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b.

S5.1 has one kernel aI+bX_v per orthonormal residual vector and s_c child calls giving C^{⊗e}. It omits the definition of C_U, s_c=W_c m-2N+2L_c, and the source/sink diagonal corrections and bank-exchange undoing, without which the telescoped operator is not C^{⊗e} on X_a->Y_a.

S2.5 (L/N<1/2 gives s<Wm) and S3 (s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, quoting that the deficits exceed 20·2^{-50}) carry the substance. The deficit values eta_b and eta_c, the extra N source ranks, and the step log m<20 are missing.
S1.1 matches Lemma lem:elementary-streams. S1.2 drops the condition that the offset must be preparable in b^{O(1)} time, as well as the prime radix and the denominators prime to q.

Both lemmas are stated faithfully (E_1 Pi E_2 with a ones; exactly a interchanges plus O(V)). The elimination proof and the three-update trick that implements each one of Pi with a single interchange are not shown.

S4's method (row-split role streams, bit network with edge shears by recursive interchanges) and S4.4's recurrence F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), giving O(Ve^tau), follow the paper. Two steps are missing: the conversion of the shear H<-H+D into the interchange (D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D), and the fixed-tape depth-first schedule that justifies the O(1) overhead.
S4 states O(Vu^tau) for u-bit fields, and S4.5 names the route (rows from high digits, base-m decomposition, radix-q padding). That is one infer step without sub-steps, so it counts as stated.

Has s_c child calls on e/m axes and the conversion to H_0^{⊗D} via diagonal phases and b^D. It lacks the binary change of basis P_M that puts residual directions on coordinate slots, the inverse-child identity, and the reduction of the rest to row additions.
Only 'packed changes of selected address bits' and 'packed address moves'. The XOR at positions rho+iK, the eight cyclic shifts, the bad set and the cost bound are absent.

S5.3 says only that 'the recursion' gives O(Vd^{lambda'}). The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), the leaves at e<d^beta and the lambda' condition are missing. S3's generic O(1)-overhead recursion does not match this one.

The statement has H_0 on one common bit per chunk for D<=d chunks, O(Vd^{lambda'}) with lambda'<1, exact dyadic intermediates, one truncation and error below sqrt2·2^{-p}. It omits K=floor(d^c) and the conditions on lambda'. The route via phase frames, conversion, packing and recursion is the paper's, but the guard-width analysis and the row construction with its recurrence are missing.

Cost O(Tp[dK+pK^{tau-1}+l d^{lambda'}]), error sqrt2·l·2^{-p}, B_tF_t^- in bit-reversed order, grouping into H and J_E, and layout charging are all correct. Character cancellation F^+F^-=t^{-1}I and the opposite procedure's counterpart F^+B^{-1}L^{-1} are not stated.
S7.1 matches the lemma: signed packing, the O(n log n) multiplier, and Q_p(fg/r) in O(rp log(rp)). The evaluation point 2^{4p} and the four products are not given, but the statement is faithful.

M_r=(f*g)/T, the error sqrt2·M(3l+1)·2^{-p} and the extra O(Tp log(rp)) are right, and S7.2 gives the retained LB order. The convolution identity F^-(f*g)=M(F^-f)(F^-g) and the final exact scale by M are missing.

The one-dimensional and tensor identities, the contractions, the error p^2 and the exposure cost are right, but the hypothesis theta>p/alpha^4 and the line-map cost are omitted. The one-dimensional identity is cited, not derived; only the tensoring step is shown.
Both identities are stated correctly, but the chirp a is not defined (a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i)), and the evenness of t_i and the conjugation route to RF^+ are not given.

S15 gives tau, sigma, lambda', epsilon and kappa correctly. The sizes b, p=6b, d, K, T, r, the remaining parameters, and the prime source lengths are absent, so the item's defining content is not there. This is the conservative verdict.
Phi: x->prod x_i^{mu_i} preserves cyclic convolution and is triangular, which is right. mu_i=P_i^{-1} mod s_i and the triangular formula b_i=a_i+mu_i sum a_jP_j are not given.
S12 has x_d->zeta y with zeta=e^{pi i/r}, turning cyclic convolution in the last axis into negacyclic ring arithmetic, as in the paper. The M_C formula is not written out.

The six steps can be read off C, S11, S10, S13 and S14: digits, Phi, two transforms, product, opposite transform, scales S and 2^{2b+4}S, rounding, carries. The composition of the source transform (A, chirp, B_0, 2^gamma) and the digit scale 2^{-b-2} are not stated, and Phi^{-1} is implicit.
S14 states that the error is below 1/2 after the two scales, so rounding is exact, followed by carries. The error chain (E_s, E_w, 448b·2^{-3b/4}) and the role of gamma<=b/4 and p=6b are missing.

S15: every normalized cost is at most p^{1-2kappa} (min g_i=2kappa), giving O(n(lg n)^{1-kappa}). The table rows, V=Tp=Theta(n), and the absorption of fixed powers of log p by the slack kappa are not given.
S0 only relies on 'nlogn-conjecture'. The liminf formulation of the negation is never stated.

errors.says: With s/W<m^tau, a call at parameter mf done by s calls at parameter f on volume V/W gives normalized cost O(f^tau). This is offered as the common recursive saving for both procedures (S5 relies on it).
errors.paper: That conclusion needs O(1) overhead per node (eq:swap-recurrence). The butterfly layer's recurrence has overhead O((eK)^tau+1) and leaves O(e) for e<d^beta, and it yields O(d^{lambda'}) with lambda'>max{lambda, sigma+beta(1-sigma)}, not O(e^tau).

errors.says: Telescoping the phase frames gives C^{⊗e} on every role by s_c child calls.
errors.paper: Telescoping alone gives C^{-1} on the 27 support coordinates on X_a->Y_a and a sign on the X outputs. C^{⊗e} on every role holds only after the source/sink Z_{a,k} corrections, the scalar i^{27k}, negation, and undoing the exchange.

chain: The tree follows the paper's route to the main bound: finite networks, frames, labels, s<Wm, matrix shears, interchange recursion, phase-frame butterfly layer, synthetic transforms, convolution, resampling and chirp, CRT and twist, recovery, and the cost table. It thins at the rank budget, where rank equal to dimension change, Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich and the N extra source ranks are missing. It thins again at the butterfly layer, where packed selected-bit addition and the layer recurrence with overhead O((eK)^tau+1) are only asserted. Exact recovery and the time table are stated without their error chain or table entries.

steps.note: The exchange (X,Y)->(-Y,X), scratch restoration and 'triple-intersection' gather/scatter are present. h=100, indexing by triples, N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3 are never given (m and N appear only as undefined symbols), so this is graded conservatively.
S2.3 gives D_out S_Omega D_in^{-1} through the commuting common frame, and S2's motivation says intermediate frames are chosen to make edges cheap.

S2.4 has nondegenerate labels in an m-dimensional bilinear space, nested on every edge, with the only decreasing edges the central wires from time 3 to 4. The loss h per such edge and F^{⊗3} are not stated.
S2's motivation says only that 'nested subspace labels make an edge's cost its dimension change'. rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U and the N rank-one source edges are missing.
L is named as the total dimension lost, but the budget Wm-2N+2L, L=Ich and s_b=W_b m-N+2L_b are absent.
S2.5 states L/N<1/2 in both networks, giving the strict deficit s<Wm, and quotes line 1110. The exact ratios 100/539 and 101/539 and the deficit N-2L are not given.
S4.3: the endpoint matrices differ by I_m, so the bit network gives H<-H+D on every role. The -P_{U_a} source is not named.
E_1 Pi E_2 factorization, a rank-a shear in exactly a interchanges plus O(V), and S4's motivation that edge ranks sum to s calls (S3: s calls per node).
S3 has children of volume V/W, s/W<m^tau with tau=1-2^{-50}, and the quote that the deficits exceed 20·2^{-50}. S4.4 has F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), so F_k=O(e^tau). The bound log m<20 is not stated.

central.summary: The plan carries the chain's skeleton: frames, nested labels with the central decrease, L<N/2 giving s<Wm, the endpoint identity, rank-many recursive interchanges, and the recurrence with tau=1-2^{-50}. The quantitative core is thin. The network's parameters (h, N, m) are missing, as is the rank-equals-dimension-change fact with its N source exceptions, and the budget Wm-2N+2L with L=Ich. So the reader is told that s<Wm, not shown why.
